client.name: Harborline Outfitters
client.about: Harborline sells outdoor gear online. Its support team of eight answers customers by email and chat, and tracks everything in SupportDesk, the early-stage platform Lanternfish is building for them.
client.contacts: Hannah Brooks (support team lead), Marcus Bell (support operations manager) and Elena Duarte (customer support supervisor) report the bugs.

project.name: SupportDesk
project.about: A two-screen support app: a ticket list with search, and a details screen where agents change status, priority and assignee. React and Vite on the front end, Node.js, Express and SQLite on the back end.
project.stack: React and Vite, Node.js and Express, SQLite

welcome.subject: Welcome to Lanternfish Labs!
welcome.body:
Hi, and welcome aboard!

I'm Rafaela, the engineering manager here. You're joining the **SupportDesk** project, which we're building for **Harborline Outfitters**. Their support team already uses it every day, so the bugs they report are real and they hurt.

Here's how we work:

- Your tickets show up on the **Board**. Take one at a time: drag it to **In Progress** when you start, and to **In QA** when you think it's fixed.
- The code lives in your workspace container. **Open in VS Code** attaches your editor to it, with Node, the terminal and the debugger already set up. Run `npm run dev` in the VS Code terminal and use **Open app in browser** to try the app.
- QA runs the project tests first, then checks the ticket itself. If something fails, the card comes back with notes.
- Stuck? Message **Priya** from the ticket. She'll point you in the right direction, one hint at a time.

When you're ready, click **Get next assignment**. I picked a nice first one for you.

Rafaela

front-1.subject: New ticket: SD-214
front-1.body:
Hannah's team flagged this one: the **Previous** and **Next** buttons on the ticket details page change the address bar, but the page keeps showing the old ticket. One agent already changed the status of the wrong ticket because of it.

It's a classic, and easy to reproduce. Take your time, reproduce it first, and check the browser DevTools.

Rafaela

front-2.subject: New ticket: SD-231
front-2.body:
Marcus sent us a worrying one: assigning a ticket to someone who left the company shows a **success** message, but nothing is saved. A customer waited three days because of it.

Read the ticket carefully: there are two separate problems in it, and QA checks both.

Rafaela

front-3.subject: New ticket: SD-238
front-3.body:
Elena reports that priority changes don't survive a page refresh. The screen says it worked, and there are no errors anywhere.

This one is about following the data, so expect to spend some time in the Network tab.

Rafaela

front-4.subject: New ticket: SD-245
front-4.body:
This one is marked **Critical**: since the latest release, some tickets open as a completely blank page. The server logs are clean, so you'll need the browser to tell you what's going on.

Priya says it's her favorite kind of bug to teach.

Rafaela

back-1.subject: New ticket: SD-252
back-1.body:
A server-side one: searching the ticket list for `%` or `_` returns every ticket. Hannah's team searches for file names like `report_final.csv` all day, so the search box is useless for them right now.

Start from the API, not the screen: `curl` is your friend here.

Rafaela

back-2.subject: New ticket: SD-257
back-2.body:
Marcus is worried, and he's right: tickets without an assignee have disappeared from the list. Those are exactly the new tickets his team triages every morning.

The answer is in how the server loads tickets from the database. Compare what the API returns with what you expect.

Rafaela

back-3.subject: New ticket: SD-263
back-3.body:
Marcus's nightly automation sent `"status": "closed"` in lowercase, and the API saved it as is. Now 38 tickets show an empty status.

This one is about validation: what the API accepts and what it actually stores.

Rafaela

back-4.subject: New ticket: SD-270
back-4.body:
**Critical**, and Priya added the `security` label: searching for a name with an apostrophe, like `O'Brien`, breaks the ticket list.

Read the server log carefully. A broken query is a sign that user input reached the SQL itself.

Rafaela

completion.subject: SupportDesk: project done!
completion.body:
You completed the whole {{track}} track of SupportDesk, so this project is done on your side. Hannah, Marcus and Elena all sent their thanks, and Harborline's support team is having a much calmer week.

You can keep going with the other tracks of SupportDesk whenever you like. New projects are on their way too.

Thanks for the effort.

Rafaela

trackCompletion.subject: The {{track}} track is done!
trackCompletion.body:
You closed every {{track}} ticket of SupportDesk. Hannah's team noticed: the queue is moving again.

Thanks for the effort.

Rafaela
